hero.lede: I'm Luis Talavera — a developer building thoughtful, performant interfaces from Arequipa, Perú.

work.lede: A short trail of products, tools and pages I've designed or shipped in the last few years.

skills.lede: Frontend by default, with enough backend, tooling and process to ship end-to-end.

about.lede: I care about how an interface feels under the finger — the rhythm of an animation, the weight of a typeface, the quiet of an empty state.
about.p1: Right now I build Svelte web components for an enterprise event platform at RainFocus — work that ships across some of the world's largest tech conferences — while also developing a Next.js B2B SaaS for lead management. Before that I worked full-stack: React front ends backed by Scala on a dealership platform, and my first role doing e-commerce on VTEX.
about.p2: I started out as a mechatronics engineer before moving into software through a full-stack bootcamp — probably why I still like understanding the system behind the surface. Outside of work I'm usually in the dev tools, the terminal, or a sketchbook trying to design before I code.

rainfocus.name: RainFocus
rainfocus.description: My current role — building Svelte web components and styling platform widgets for an enterprise event-management suite. The work has shipped across events for Salesforce (Dreamforce, World Tour, Agentforce, TDX), ServiceNow (Knowledge, World Forum), Zscaler (Zenith Live), Anyscale (Ray Summit), Workday (Rising, DevCon), Autodesk (GEMS), and Meta, GitHub, Jamf and IBM, among others.

leadcadi.name: Leadcadi
leadcadi.description: Frontend for a lead & campaign management platform built on Next.js. I work with Server and Client Components, dynamic filtering and controlled forms, collaborating closely with the design and backend teams.

dealerpro.name: DealerPro
dealerpro.description: Full-stack work on a dealership management system. I built the React interfaces and integrated the Scala APIs, also contributing to the backend with Play Framework and to frontend architecture and usability.

footloose.name: Footloose
footloose.description: Where I started — frontend on the Footloose e-commerce store. Redesigns and new landing pages on VTEX, plus custom React components when the defaults fell short, and email design in markdown.

codeable.name: Codeable evaluation
codeable.description: Owned the React frontend of the registration + evaluation flow for Codeable applicants. Scored coding and English: timed attempts, an embedded code editor, retry logic. The Ruby on Rails API handled the heavy validation.

frontend.name: Frontend
frontend.description: React and Svelte for interactive surfaces — including reusable web components — with TypeScript for guard rails and SCSS or Tailwind for systems. I care a lot about the small details: focus rings, scroll behavior, prefers-reduced-motion.

backend.name: Backend
backend.description: A full-stack background: I've integrated and contributed to Scala APIs on Play Framework, and built apps with Ruby on Rails. Comfortable owning a small API end-to-end and speaking the backend's language.

github.name: GitHub & CI
github.description: Long-time Git user, including GitHub Actions for CI, GitHub Pages for static deploys (this site, included). Clean histories, reviewable PRs, conventional commits where it fits.

agile.name: Agile
agile.description: Trained in Scrum and shipped against it in teams. Funny enough, I'd been running sprint-shaped weeks with classmates before I knew the name for it. Process should serve the team — not the other way around.
